# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
<!-- Generated from skill/agents/ at build time. Do not edit; edit the agent definition. -->
This harness has no subagent capability, so you are running this role inline. Step fully out of the work you just finished, adopt only this file's instructions for the pass, and disclose the substitution in one line when you report. Where the text below addresses a parent agent, you are both parties: produce the full output contract first, then act on it yourself.

# Impeccable Finish Reviewer

You are the finishing reviewer for an Impeccable build: fresh eyes on a done artifact, outside the build thread's attention gravity. You edit nothing; the parent applies your fixes.

You have no browser. Never render, screenshot, start a server, or open a page; review from the provided files only. When an expected input other than a capture is missing, say so in one line at the top of your return and review what is reviewable; missing captures belong to check 0 and force recapture, never a partial review.

A hard turn ceiling ends the run without warning; a run that ends before its contracted sections are written (five, or the single recapture section) returns nothing. Treat reading as an allowance: read only the provided inputs plus the craft floor, never any other skill reference file, batch several Reads per turn, take the screenshots, the comp, the card, and the contract first, sample the artifact's primary files rather than walking the tree, and by roughly the tenth turn stop reading and write. Name whatever went unread in the line above the sections.

## Input Contract

Expect: the original request; the confirmed user answers; the artifact path(s); the screenshots the parent captured, in `.impeccable/review/` (web: `desktop.png` and `mobile.png`; native: device-class names such as `phone.png` and `tablet.png`, suffixed per OS on adaptive). A screenshot path the calling brief names is authoritative when the file exists; `.impeccable/review/` is where to look when the brief names none or a named path is missing, never a filename you invent. Also expect: the direction contract (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM); the PRODUCT.md path; existing hook or detector findings; the chosen world's QUALITY BAR card paths; on a comp-led build the approved comp path (a code-led build has none; it passes the chosen decision comp as a separate critique-reference input, labeled as such, and nothing here that binds "the approved comp" binds it); on a comp-led build the build state (`.impeccable/build/state.json`), the measured spec (`.impeccable/build/spec.json`), and the diff directories `.impeccable/review/diff/hero/` and `.impeccable/review/diff/final/` (each holds `side-by-side.png`, `heatmap.png`, `regions/<id>.png` paired crops, and `report.json` with per-region scores and verdicts from `impeccable comp-diff`); and the skill's `reference/craft-floor.md` path. On a native (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`) build the packet adds the platform reference path(s) (`reference/ios.md` / `reference/android.md`) and a line saying no detector ran: read the platform reference alongside the craft floor, judge every check in the platform's own conventions, treat the screenshots as device captures, and know your floor check is the build's only slop gate. When the harness can view images, open the screenshots, the comp, and the card first, and inventory the comp's salient elements in your own words before reading the direction contract or any builder-authored summary: a review anchored on the contract inherits whatever the builder's abstraction dropped.

## Checks, in order

0. **Evidence.** Before any other check, verify the required captures exist and every capture is valid. Required: the platform's full viewport set (web: `desktop.png` and `mobile.png`; native: one capture per shipped device class), plus every capture the calling brief names as required, a reported user viewport (`user-<width>.png`) included. Valid: no black or blank regions, content matching what the filename claims (a visit capture showing the About section is invalid), the document top visible where the file claims a full page, dimensions that make sense for the named viewport. A required capture that is absent fails exactly like one that is malformed: a viewport nobody captured is a viewport nobody inspected, and it cannot ship. When any capture fails, the whole review changes shape: return `disposition: recapture` as the first line, then one section, `recapture`, listing each missing or invalid file and what a valid capture of it shows, and stop. Never build a matrix on malformed evidence; a verdict derived from a broken capture launders the breakage into an approval, and the parent owes you a full re-review on valid captures, not a scoring round.
1. **Persistence.** PRODUCT.md exists. On a comp-led build, `.impeccable/build/state.json` exists and every phase before `review` is `closed` or explicitly `skipped`; an open or failed phase is a material finding. A comp-led config with no state file, or a state whose `comps` phase is neither `closed` nor `skipped`, means the comp round was skipped and the build ran from a world description alone, a material finding that outranks craft; a phase closed with a `forced` record is disclosed as a material finding unless the user downgraded the comp in words the packet quotes; a state file whose `hero.gate.score` sits under 0.72, or a missing state file, means the reproduction ran unproven, a material finding, and `.impeccable/review/hero-repro.png` must exist either way. When DESIGN.md predates this build (an extension or redesign), it matches the built world; on a new world it is written after this review by the documenter, so its absence here is not a finding. When comp-round comps exist under `.impeccable/mocks/`, an approval record exists too: the surface brief naming the approved comp, or an `approved` flag in its sidecar. Comp-round comps with no recorded pick mean the approval point was skipped, a material finding. Files under `.impeccable/mocks/decision/` are exempt: they are the direction round's dealt hand, produced before any comp round, and imply no approval whatever the build path; a code-led build has no comp round at all.
2. **Fidelity.** Start from the measurement, then judge what it cannot: read `.impeccable/review/diff/final/report.json` (and hero) first; every region scored `missing` or `contradicted` is a matrix row in that state unless the paired crop under `regions/` shows the score is wrong, and you say why; a region scored `match` still gets your eye for lettering character and material, which the numbers do not measure. Then, against your own element inventory of the approved comp, never against the contract's summary of it: topology, reading order, focal scale, overlaps and z-order, density, signature geometry, the primary action's treatment (a CTA the comp physically works, dissolves, or stamps is a signature element; its plain-rectangle rendition is contradicted), navigation items and icons, headline levels and scale relationships. Classify every salient element: match, acceptable adaptation, missing, contradicted, or added without approval. Three rows are mandatory in every matrix. TYPE: the display lettering's character, compression, width, weight, contrast, terminals, against the comp's; a face of a different character is contradicted however the layout matches. MATERIAL: an element rendered as flat CSS or clean vector where the comp shows painted, textured, dimensional, or photographic material is contradicted regardless of placement; medium is part of the promise. GROUND: the page field's value and temperature against the comp's, sampled from pixels on both sides when tooling allows rather than judged from memory, and read as the net on-screen result where a texture or tile paints over the base color; a ground warmer or cooler than the comp's is contradicted however faithfully the layout matches, and drift toward the rendition prior (warm cream on light grounds, blue-black slate on dark) is the direction to hunt. With no approved comp, TYPE and MATERIAL do not lapse: judge them against the contract's OWN-WORLD and the world's real materials, and treat faked physicality (CSS bevels, embossing, stamped-metal or chalk effects imitating a material the page never renders) as contradicted on its face; imitation material is the single most reliable mark of machine-made design. GROUND narrows rather than lapses: with no comp to sample, a color OWN-WORLD names is the target and the same warmer-or-cooler judgment applies; when OWN-WORLD names none, there is no GROUND authority, and the review says so in place of a verdict, because a target the reviewer invents turns the check into taste. A critique-reference comp on such a build is provocation, not spec: no element matrix, no adaptation citations, no asset obligations; its one contribution is what the image dared that the build did not, and dares worth adopting enter material_fixes as ordinary ordered fixes. An adaptation counts as intentional only when it cites the user answer, surface brief, accessibility need, or product truth that forced it; an uncited deviation is a defect. A missing signature element, a changed topology, or content added without approval fails fidelity and outranks every craft point in material_fixes. When MATERIAL is contradicted on the focal element, or contradiction is the page rather than the exception, stop ordering repairs: make the first material fix a rebuild directive naming the comp regions to re-derive and the assets to produce; a list of patches against a rejected page launders the rejection into an approval. A fix that requires producing an asset says so explicitly ("produce: <region> as a raster asset"), never phrased as a style adjustment the parent will answer with CSS. The comp is the spec for composition, topology, element inventory, density, lettering character, and material; it is not a pixel spec for semantics, accessibility, or responsive reflow, and that allowance covers translation, never replacement.
3. **Ceiling.** Against the QUALITY BAR card: name the world's native devices the build left unused, frame, depth, lettering treatment, ornament density, motion. The card governs commitment and finish, never composition.
4. **Contract, promise by promise.** First verify FORM carries the seed reference the concept roll printed (`seed:` and 16 hex), corroborated against the roll output the parent saw or with `impeccable concept-seed --check-seed <reference>` (exit 0 means this machine rolled it). A raw seed key in FORM is itself a material fix: the brief is committed, and the key must not be. `seed: none (unavailable)` stands only when the roll printed SEED REFERENCE unavailable, which `--check-seed none` confirms with exit 0. Any other contract with no reference, or one neither source corroborates, means the roll was skipped, a material fix ahead of any craft point. Then, for each of the five blocks: does the render keep the promise? Apply the memory test to the first viewport.
5. **Truth.** Demonstration data authored and labeled synthetic; no invented commercial claims; unanswered claims present as marked placeholders, not omissions. Every raster region of the spec shipped as its plate (the spec names the file; the page references it; the region's diff row is not `missing`), not a gradient, an inline SVG, or a many-vertex `clip-path` standing in for it, and every produced asset visibly present in the screenshots; an asset applied at near-zero opacity or buried behind a wash is a compliance token, not a shipped material, and the detector's `buried-raster` and `organic-clip-path` findings in the packet are material fixes.
6. **Floor.** Read the craft floor's Refuse list and hold the screenshots against it: kickers and eyebrows, hard offset shadows outside a neobrutalist world, glyph icons, system display faces, gradient text, side stripes, and the rest. A banned element is a material fix even when it matches nothing in the comp: the builder loaded the same ban before writing it, and fidelity to a comp cannot authorize what the floor refuses. The parent's hook findings cover this mechanically where hooks run; this check exists because hookless harnesses reach you with none, and on those harnesses a banned element you miss ships.

Do not run a second detector pass; mechanical findings belong to the parent's hooks.

## Disposition

The first line of your return is `disposition: recapture`, `disposition: rebuild`, `disposition: fix`, or `disposition: ship`. These four words are the whole vocabulary; never invent another. # Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

<!-- Generated from skill/agents/ at build time. Do not edit; edit the agent definition. -->
This harness has no subagent capability, so you are running this role inline. Step fully out of the work you just finished, adopt only this file's instructions for the pass, and disclose the substitution in one line when you report. Where the text below addresses a parent agent, you are both parties: produce the full output contract first, then act on it yourself.

# Impeccable Documenter

You record a project's design system after the build is done. Ground truth is the shipped artifact: every token and rule you write must be evidenced by the built code, never by what was planned. Writing the system after the fact is the point; a rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it.

Complete the check within your turn ceiling. Batch Reads, take `reference/document.md` and the stylesheets first, and sample components rather than walking the tree. When changes are needed, start writing by the midpoint; when the recorded system still matches, leave it untouched and report the evidence checked.

## Input Contract

Expect: the project root; the artifact path(s); the direction contract text (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM); PRODUCT.md path; the path to the skill's `reference/document.md`; and the boundary to write at (project or app root). An existing DESIGN.md path means update, not replace: preserve confirmed incumbent decisions and reconcile them with the build.

## Workflow

1. Read `reference/document.md` in full; it is the operating spec for DESIGN.md's format, token schema, sidecar, and section order. Follow it exactly.
2. Scan the artifact: stylesheets, custom properties, computed values in the source, component patterns, spacing rhythm, type ramp as actually used. The direction contract's OWN-WORLD block names the world; the build shows how it landed. Where they diverge, the build wins and the prose may note the divergence.
3. For a new world or approved system change, write DESIGN.md and its sidecar from durable, reused rules in the build. Ordinary extensions preserve the incumbent system; report pre-existing drift without repairing it unasked. Do not write merely to prove this pass ran.
4. Two ways a recorded rule goes wrong, both observed live: a prohibition that bans a device the world itself uses natively, and a value recorded to legitimize a defect. Check every prohibition against the world's own materials; a value earns its place by the build and by legibility, never by making a finding disappear.
5. Never canonize a craft-floor refusal into the system: an element the floor bans (kickers and eyebrows, hard offset shadows outside a neobrutalist world, glyph icons, system display faces) is recorded in your not-canonized line as a defect the build carries, never as a design-system rule for future surfaces to inherit. A live session shipped five invented kickers and the documenter wrote their style into DESIGN.md; that is how one violation becomes the house style.

## Output Contract

Return: paths written, or “No changes” with the source and system files checked; a five-line system summary (palette, type ramp, named rules); and one line naming defects or drift not canonized or repaired, and why. No other prose.416 document.md
Generate a `DESIGN.md` file at the project root that captures the current visual design system, so AI agents generating new screens stay on-brand.

DESIGN.md follows the [official DESIGN.md format spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-labs-code/design.md/main/docs/spec.md): optional YAML frontmatter carrying machine-readable design tokens, followed by up to eight markdown sections in a fixed order. **Tokens are normative; prose provides context for how to apply them.** Sections may be omitted when not relevant, but those present stay in the specified order. Use the canonical headings below so the file remains portable across DESIGN.md-aware tools.

## The frontmatter: token schema

The YAML frontmatter is the machine-readable layer. It's what Stitch's linter validates and what the live panel renders tiles from. Keep it tight; every entry should correspond to a token the project actually uses.

```yaml
---
name: <project title>
description: <one-line tagline>
colors:
  primary: "#b8422e"
  neutral-bg: "#faf7f2"
  # ...one entry per extracted color; key = descriptive slug
typography:
  display:
    fontFamily: "Cormorant Garamond, Georgia, serif"
    fontSize: "clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 4.5rem)"
    fontWeight: 300
    lineHeight: 1
    letterSpacing: "normal"
  body:
    # ...
rounded:
  sm: "4px"
  md: "8px"
spacing:
  sm: "8px"
  md: "16px"
components:
  button-primary:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.primary}"
    textColor: "{colors.neutral-bg}"
    rounded: "{rounded.sm}"
    padding: "16px 48px"
  button-primary-hover:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.primary-deep}"
---
```

Rules that matter:

- **Token refs** use `{path.to.token}` (e.g. `{colors.primary}`, `{rounded.md}`). Components may reference primitives; primitives may not reference each other.
- **Colors accept any valid CSS color string.** Hex is the recommended default for portability, but preserve an incumbent `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()`, wide-gamut, or mixed-color value when it is the project's normative source. Never split the source of truth without explicit reason.
- **Component sub-tokens** are limited to 8 props: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `typography`, `rounded`, `padding`, `size`, `height`, `width`. Shadows, motion, focus rings, backdrop-filter: none of those fit. Carry them in the sidecar (Step 4b).
- **Scale keys are open-ended.** Use whatever names the project already uses (`oxblood-deep`, `surface-container-low`). Don't rename to Material defaults.
- **Variants are naming convention, not schema.** `button-primary` / `button-primary-hover` / `button-primary-active` as sibling keys.

## The markdown body: eight sections (canonical order)

1. `## Overview`
2. `## Colors`
3. `## Typography`
4. `## Layout`
5. `## Elevation & Depth`
6. `## Shapes`
7. `## Components`
8. `## Do's and Don'ts`

Omit irrelevant sections rather than filling them with invented rules. Put responsive layout in Layout, depth in Elevation & Depth, radius and form language in Shapes, and per-component behavior in Components. Unknown sections are preserved by the format, but new visual guidance should use the canonical structure whenever it fits.

## When to run

- New-work found a coherent incumbent visual system but no `DESIGN.md`.
- The first implementation of a new world is complete and its provisional decisions need to be carbonized.
- An existing `DESIGN.md` is stale (the design has drifted).
- Before a large redesign, to capture the current state as a reference.

If a `DESIGN.md` already exists, **do not silently overwrite it**. Show the user the existing file first. Ask with Codex's structured user-input/question tool when available, or directly in chat if it is not, and wait for the answer before continuing. The choice is refresh, overwrite, or merge.

## Two paths

- **Scan mode** (default): the project has design tokens, components, or rendered output. Extract, then confirm descriptive language. Use when there's code to analyze.
- **Seed mode**: the project is pre-implementation. Ensure PRODUCT.md exists, then reuse new-work's visual-world workshop and write its directional DESIGN.md seed. Re-run in scan mode once there's code.

Decide by scanning first (Scan mode Step 1). If the scan finds no tokens, no component files, and no rendered site, offer seed mode; don't silently switch. `$impeccable document --seed` requests new-work's world workshop, but it does not authorize replacing coherent code: when an incumbent system exists, offer scan mode or route an explicit identity-replacement request through new-work.

## Scan mode (approach C: auto-extract, then confirm descriptive language)

### Step 1: Find the design assets

Search the codebase in priority order:

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

> Every fact below is inferred from the written product brief. No interview took place: the benchmark run authorises inferring audience, design and implementation decisions from the brief alone. Items marked _(inferred)_ are the builder's reading, not a confirmed answer.

## Platform

web

## Stack

delegated: Vite + TypeScript with no UI framework, three.js for the 3D view, `bun test` with happy-dom for tests. Chosen because the brief demands a self-contained static `dist/`, a `BASE_PATH`-aware build and a fast interpreter test loop; a framework would add weight without solving a problem this app has. _(inferred)_

## Users

- Polish-speaking learners writing their first programs: primary and early secondary pupils, at a school computer-lab desktop or at home, sometimes on a phone. Their job is to type a short program, run it, see the turtle draw and fix what went wrong. _(inferred)_
- Teachers who set drawing tasks and want pupils to check their own work and hand in a picture or a link. _(inferred)_
- Adults who learned Logo in Polish school labs and come back for the feeling of it, then stay because 3D is new. _(inferred)_

## Product Purpose

Logomocja is a Polish-language studio for turtle drawing: write a Logo program, run it, watch the turtle draw on a plane (2D) or in space (3D). It is complete on its own: a learner can read what the language can do, run the thirteen standard programs, write their own, solve the challenges and share the result. Success is a learner going from an empty editor to a drawing they made, and understanding every error message on the way.

## Positioning

A faithful Polish Logo dialect (accented and unaccented keywords, English aliases, `oto … już` procedures) that runs a real 3D turtle with pitch and roll, where any flat program draws the identical shape in both modes. It runs with no account, no backend and no network.

## Operating Context

- School labs with shared desktops and keyboards; home laptops; phones for showing a drawing to someone. _(inferred)_
- Programs travel as permalinks (URL encodes program and mode), as `.logo` text files, and drawings as PNG exports. _(brief)_
- Drafts survive reloads per mode in local storage only. _(brief)_
- Deployed as a static site, possibly under a sub-path (`BASE_PATH`), with hash routing so a refresh on any page works without rewrites. _(brief)_

## Capabilities and Constraints

- Fixed language semantics (lexing, expressions with whitespace-sensitive binary operators, repeat with lexical `nrpowt`, variables with parse-time declaration checks, conditionals, procedures, limits). The interpreter must be exact; it is tested through `window.logomocja.run(source, mode)`. _(brief)_
- Fixed feature list: editor with highlighting, error marker and execution highlight; run/step/pause/resume/reset with speed; 2D pan/zoom/fit/origin; 3D orbit/pan/zoom/reset/grid/axes with a WebGL fallback message; 13 standard examples verbatim; at least five auto-checked challenges with persisted progress; permalink, PNG export, `.logo` download/open; a Polish command reference; per-mode drafts; keyboard shortcuts; responsive, light/dark, keyboard-operable. _(brief)_
- Testing hook `window.logomocja` with `version`, `run`, `open`. _(brief)_
- Terminology is Polish: żółw (turtle), pisak (pen), polecenie (command), procedura, zmienna, powtórz, wyzwanie (challenge), szkic (draft). _(inferred)_

## Brand Commitments

- Name: Logomocja. Interface language: Polish. _(brief)_
- The turtle's default pen colour `#16866a` and the standard programs' colours (`#c1763d`, `#2b6fb3`, `#a478c0`, `#6b4f2a`, `#2f8f4e`) are part of the shipped content and must render exactly. _(brief)_
- Nostalgia for the classic Polish Logo environment of the same name, without copying its look; it should feel good to use today. _(brief)_

## Evidence on Hand

- The thirteen standard programs with names, modes and one-line descriptions, shipped byte for byte. _(brief)_
- No testimonials, school adoption figures, curriculum endorsements or user counts exist; none may be invented.

## Product Principles

1. The drawing is the feedback: every action ends in something visible on the canvas, quickly. _(inferred)_
2. Errors teach: one precise Polish sentence, the exact line and column, and nothing drawn that the learner did not ask for. _(inferred)_
3. Never lose a learner's work: drafts persist per mode and nothing overwrites an unsaved draft silently. _(brief)_
4. One program, one shape: flat programs agree in 2D and 3D, so 3D is a step up, not a different language. _(brief)_
5. Works anywhere: offline, no account, desktop and phone. _(brief)_

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Every control keyboard-operable and labelled with visible focus; light and dark themes following the system with a manual toggle; usable on a phone-sized screen. Young readers: plain Polish, no jargon in messages. _(brief + inferred)_

Someone who uses tools like this one should know where everything is before they notice the world. The world lends four things and only these: type, palette, density, and one signature move. Read every candidate, the assigned direction, and every challenger through that limit before you fuse or judge it. Read every candidate, the assigned direction, and every challenger through that limit before you fuse or judge it. # Surface: Logomocja studio (index.html, all hash routes)

Scope: the whole single-page app: studio (editor + 2D/3D view + run controls), examples, challenges, command reference (`#/pomoc`). Visitor mode: **Operate** for the studio, examples and challenges; the reference route is a **Read** surface inside the same frame.

Audience and job: Polish learners (and their teachers, and returning adults) write a Logo program, run or step it, watch the turtle draw, fix errors, solve challenges, share the result. Constraints: fixed language and feature list from the product brief, offline static site, desktop and phone.

Decision record: no interview; direction taken from the concept roll without a decision page (benchmark authorises unattended inference). Code-led (Operate surface; no image generation). Telemetry ping skipped (telemetry off, no user consent channel).

## Direction contract

THESIS: The studio is a printed cut-and-fold model sheet in the Mały Modelarz tradition: the drawing area is the sheet, the program is the assembly instruction, and a flat program "folds" into the same shape in 3D. It refuses the category default of a candy-coloured kids' coding app with a cartoon turtle, and the dark neon IDE.

OWN-WORLD: Cool card-stock ground, white printed sheet for the canvas in both themes (dimmed, never inverted, at night), near-black key-line ink. The shell header is a committed band of the turtle's own ink green (#16866a). One spot-colour wheel taken from the standard programs (green #16866a, copper #c1763d, blue #2b6fb3, lilac #a478c0, umber #6b4f2a) colours the command families everywhere they appear: editor highlighting, reference sections, command chips. Line notation carries meaning: a solid line is drawn, a dashed line is a fold, meaning not-yet or pen-up. Archivo grotesque for UI (condensed width for sheet labels and part numbers), JetBrains Mono for code only. Flat colour, hairline rules, no gradients, grain or glass.

STORY: The learner sees at once where to type, what Run does, and where the turtle draws. Every run ends on the sheet; an error is one Polish sentence pinned to the exact token. Examples and challenges are sheets to open, never dead ends.

FIRST VIEWPORT: Desktop: a green header band (wordmark, 2D/3D switch, Studio · Przykłady · Wyzwania · Pomoc, theme toggle). Below it the editor sits on the left at about 42% with line numbers, and a single run toolbar sits above it: Uruchom is the one reversed plate, then Krok, Pauza/Wznów, Od nowa and the speed slider. On the right is the sheet: crop marks at its corners, the origin drawn as a printer's registration mark, the turtle marker, zoom/fit controls, and along its foot the sheet imprint. Phone: header, sheet (about 45vh), toolbar, editor, stacked.

FORM: Grounded candidate 7 of 7 (ordered: zeszyt w kratkę, tablica i przybory, wycinanki, plansze dydaktyczne, ilustracja PRL, spirograf, Mały Modelarz). seed:62a97cc46c9d2b5d. Signature move: **the sheet imprint**, the canvas margin read like a model sheet's imprint: the drawing's name, mode, scale from zoom ("skala 2:1"), segment count, and a colour-control bar of the pen colours actually used. The challenge target shows as dashed fold lines under the learner's drawing; a pen-up turtle shows a dashed outline. Raises from declined challengers:
- Raise (rw-manual-acetate-tab-board): one hue per division of the language, the same hue wherever that division appears.
- Raise (rw-timetable-slide-rack): exactly one opaque reversed plate per screen, the primary action; rank otherwise comes from weight and rule, not more colour.
- Raise (variable-font-specimen): the drawing carries the colour; chrome stays flat and ranks by scale contrast.
- Raise (aww2-zoo-gardens-guide-map): flat, unmodulated colour fields only.
- Raise (emigre-bitmap-specimen): zoom moves in whole scale steps (1:4 … 8:1) that the imprint names honestly.
- Raise (pop-culture-shelf-character-goods-catalog): every example and challenge carries the same fixed anatomy (sheet thumbnail, name, mode, one-line note, state).
Motion grammar: 150–200 ms state transitions; the only authored motion is the turtle itself drawing.

FINISH: unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance

# Logomocja

A Polish-language web studio for turtle drawing, inspired by the classic Polish Logo environment of the same name. You write a Logo program, run it or step through it, and watch the turtle draw on a plane (2D) or in space (3D). The app includes a command reference, the thirteen standard programs, ten auto-checked challenges, permalinks, PNG export and `.logo` files. It needs no account, no backend and no network at runtime.

## Run, build, test

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh) (tested with 1.4).

```sh
bun install          # dependencies
bun run dev          # development server (Vite) at http://localhost:5173
bun run build        # type-check, then build the static site into dist/
bun run preview      # serve dist/ locally
bun run test         # interpreter, runner, checker and app tests (bun test + happy-dom)
```

`dist/` is plain static files: `index.html`, hashed JS/CSS chunks, self-hosted fonts and a favicon. It contains no server code and makes no runtime network requests.

### Serving from a sub-path

The build honours `BASE_PATH` (default `/`):

```sh
BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/ bun run build
```

The resulting `dist/` works when copied to that sub-path on any static host without rewrite rules. All routes are hash routes (`#/`, `#/przyklady`, `#/przyklady/gwiazda`, `#/wyzwania`, `#/wyzwania/kwadrat`, `#/pomoc`, `#/pomoc/procedury`, `#/program?tryb=2d&kod=…`), so refreshing any page works.

## Testing hook

Once the page has loaded, `window.logomocja` provides:

- `version`: a string.
- `run(source, mode)`: interprets `source` in `"2d"` or `"3d"` without touching the UI, and returns `{ segments, error }`.
- `open(source, mode)`: loads `source` into the editor in that mode (an unsaved draft goes to the backups, exactly as when a user pastes over it), runs it to the end without animation, fits the view, and resolves to the same `{ segments, error }` once the drawing is on screen.

## What is where

```
src/lang/          the interpreter: lexer, parser (all parse-time checks), step-able executor, turtle geometry, limits
src/app/           app shell, hash router, runner (run/step/pause/resume/reset/halt), scheduler, storage, permalinks
src/editor/        CodeMirror 6 editor: whole-document highlighting, inline error marker, execution highlight
src/views/         2D sheet (canvas: pan, zoom ladder, fit, origin mark) and 3D view (three.js, loaded only with WebGL)
src/challenges/    the drawing checker
src/content/       the 13 standard programs (verbatim), the challenges, the Polish command reference
src/ui/            studio, examples, challenges and reference pages, toasts, icons, theme toggle
src/styles/        design tokens and styles
tests/             bun tests
```

## Tests and what they cover

Tests are written against four public seams, one behaviour at a time:

| Seam | Covers | Does not cover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interpreter, `run(source, mode)` (`tests/interpreter.test.ts`, `tests/examples.test.ts`) | 2D and 3D strokes, aliases, expressions and the spacing rule, variables and scope, conditionals, procedures, `stop`, `nrpowt`, every error class with line and column, all limits, the standard programs, 2D/3D parity | Anything in the browser |
| Execution controller, `createRunner` (`tests/runner.test.ts`) | Run at speed, step, pause, resume, reset, halt on edit, instant runs, parse errors vs run-time errors | Rendering, animation smoothness |
| Challenge checker, `checkAttempt` (`tests/checker.test.ts`) | Tolerance (order, direction, split strokes, position, mirror, rounding), reasons (size, missing or extra lines, colour, required commands, errors), every shipped challenge's solution passing | Whether the tasks are pedagogically well chosen |
| App in happy-dom, `mountApp` + `window.logomocja` (`tests/app.test.ts`) | `open()` agreeing with `run()`, toolbar controls, keyboard shortcuts, inline error marker and message, editing while running, examples (by gallery and by name), draft preservation and restore, per-mode drafts and theme surviving a reload, permalinks, `.logo` download/open, challenge pass/fail/progress, the reference documenting every command with a working example, the no-WebGL notice, accessible names on every control | Visual layout, colour and contrast as rendered, the 3D view itself (happy-dom has no canvas or WebGL), PNG export, real touch gestures |

### Verification limits

The container this was built in has no browser. The UI was never rendered and screenshotted in a real browser, and the three.js view was never displayed. What was verified instead:

- The production bundle was executed in happy-dom under a `BASE_PATH` sub-path, and `window.logomocja.open` matched `run` for all thirteen standard programs.
- Every asset URL in the sub-path build resolves on a plain static server.
- The 2D canvas renderer (the app's real paint code) was rendered to PNG with a headless Canvas 2D library and inspected.
- The 3D turtle's orientation maths was checked numerically.

## Design

`PRODUCT.md` records the product context. `DESIGN.md` and `.impeccable/design.json` record the visual system (a printed cut-and-fold model sheet), written after the build from the shipped code. `.impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md` holds the direction contract.

Once the page has loaded, `window.logomocja` provides:

- `version`: a string.
- `run(source, mode)`: interprets `source` in `"2d"` or `"3d"` without touching the UI, and returns `{ segments, error }`.
- `open(source, mode)`: loads `source` into the editor in that mode (an unsaved draft goes to the backups, exactly as when a user pastes over it), runs it to the end without animation, fits the view, and resolves to the same `{ segments, error }` once the drawing is on screen.

## What is where

```
src/lang/          the interpreter: lexer, parser (all parse-time checks), step-able executor, turtle geometry, limits
src/app/           app shell, hash router, runner (run/step/pause/resume/reset/halt), scheduler, storage, permalinks
src/editor/        CodeMirror 6 editor: whole-document highlighting, inline error marker, execution highlight
src/views/         2D sheet (canvas: pan, zoom ladder, fit, origin mark) and 3D view (three.js, loaded only with WebGL)
src/challenges/    the drawing checker
src/content/       the 13 standard programs (verbatim), the challenges, the Polish command reference
src/ui/            studio, examples, challenges and reference pages, toasts, icons, theme toggle
src/styles/        design tokens and styles
tests/             bun tests
```

## Tests and what they cover

Tests are written against four public seams, one behaviour at a time:

| Seam | Covers | Does not cover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interpreter, `run(source, mode)` (`tests/interpreter.test.ts`, `tests/examples.test.ts`) | 2D and 3D strokes, aliases, expressions and the spacing rule, variables and scope, conditionals, procedures, `stop`, `nrpowt`, every error class with line and column, all limits, the standard programs, 2D/3D parity | Anything in the browser |
| Execution controller, `createRunner` (`tests/runner.test.ts`) | Run at speed, step, pause, resume, reset, halt on edit, instant runs, parse errors vs run-time errors | Rendering, animation smoothness |
| Challenge checker, `checkAttempt` (`tests/checker.test.ts`) | Tolerance (order, direction, split strokes, position, mirror, rounding), reasons (size, missing or extra lines, colour, required commands, errors), every shipped challenge's solution passing | Whether the tasks are pedagogically well chosen |
| App in happy-dom, `mountApp` + `window.logomocja` (`tests/app.test.ts`) | `open()` agreeing with `run()`, toolbar controls, keyboard shortcuts, inline error marker and message, editing while running, examples (by gallery and by name), draft preservation and restore, per-mode drafts and theme surviving a reload, permalinks, `.logo` download/open, challenge pass/fail/progress, the reference documenting every command with a working example, the no-WebGL notice, accessible names on every control | Visual layout, colour and contrast as rendered, the 3D view itself (happy-dom has no canvas or WebGL), PNG export, real touch gestures |

### Verification limits

The container this was built in has no browser. The UI was never rendered and screenshotted in a real browser, and the three.js view was never displayed. What was verified instead:

- The production bundle was executed in happy-dom under a `BASE_PATH` sub-path, and `window.logomocja.open` matched `run` for all thirteen standard programs.
- Every asset URL in the sub-path build resolves on a plain static server.
- The 2D canvas renderer (the app's real paint code) was rendered to PNG with a headless Canvas 2D library and inspected.
- The 3D turtle's orientation maths was checked numerically.

## Design

`PRODUCT.md` records the product context. `DESIGN.md` and `.impeccable/design.json` record the visual system (a printed cut-and-fold model sheet), written after the build from the shipped code. `.impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md` holds the direction contract.

- **Focus Blue** (`focus`): every focus ring, 2px solid.

- **Don't** add a second reversed plate or a second accent colour to chrome.

# Design System: Logomocja

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "The Model Sheet"**

Logomocja is set like a page from a Polish cut-and-fold model magazine (the *Mały Modelarz* tradition): a white printed sheet lying on cool card stock, black key-line ink, a handful of flat spot colours, and the small print furniture of the press. That means crop marks at the corners, a registration mark at the origin, and an imprint line along the foot of the sheet. A flat sheet that folds into a solid is exactly the product's promise: a flat program draws the same shape in 2D and in 3D.

It is an Operate surface first. Someone who has used any code editor knows where everything is before they notice the world: editor on the left, run toolbar above it, sheet on the right, standard buttons, tabs, sliders and menus. The world lends four things only: type (Archivo with its condensed widths, JetBrains Mono for code), palette (card, paper, ink, one green band and the spot-colour wheel), density (compact tool chrome around a generous sheet), and one signature move, the sheet imprint. The drawing carries the colour; chrome stays flat and ranks by scale and weight.

The brief's colours are law. The turtle's default ink `#16866a` and the standard programs' colours render exactly, which is why the sheet stays paper in both themes.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Cool card-stock ground, white sheet, near-black key-line ink; one committed band of the turtle's green.
- One spot-colour wheel (green, copper, blue, lilac, umber) shared by command families everywhere.
- Print furniture as working UI: crop marks, registration-mark origin, the imprint with a colour-control bar.
- Line notation carries meaning: solid is drawn, dashed is a fold (pen up, target, not yet).
- Flat colour, hairline rules, one soft paper shadow; no gradients, grain or glass.

## Colors

A restrained neutral system tinted green-grey, with one committed band and a spot-colour wheel that does real jobs: command families, axes, states.

### Primary
- **Turtle Ink Green** (`band`): the header band behind the wordmark and navigation, and the turtle's default pen. In dark mode the band deepens to `band-dark`; the pen colour never changes.
- **Key-Line Ink Plate** (`plate`): the single reversed plate on a screen, the «Uruchom» button. In dark mode the plate inverts to `plate-dark` with dark text.

### Secondary
- **The Spot Wheel** (`spot-green`, `spot-copper`, `spot-blue`, `spot-lilac`, `spot-umber`): the standard programs' colours. They give the 3D axes (X copper, Y green, Z blue) and the mode chips. As darker, text-safe variants they give the command-family hues: `fam-move` (np, ws, dom), `fam-turn` (pw, lw, góra, dół, pp, pl), `fam-pen` (pod, opu, kolor, grubość, czyść), `fam-control` (powtórz, jeśli, jeżeli, stop, nrpowt) and `fam-define` (oto, już, niech, procedure names).

### Neutral
- **Card Stock** (`ground`): the app ground between panels; the margin the sheet's crop marks sit in.
- **Printed Paper** (`paper`, `paper-2`, `paper-3`): editor panel, toolbars and gutter, then hover and inline-code fills.
- **Key-Line Ink** (`ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`): text, secondary text and tertiary text. `ink-3` is the lightest text allowed and holds 4.5:1 on paper and gutter.
- **Hairline Rules** (`rule`, `rule-2`): 1px dividers and control borders.
- **The Sheet** (`sheet`, `sheet-dark`, `sheet-rule`, `sheet-ghost`): the drawing surface, its grid and the dashed challenge target.

### States
- **Focus Blue** (`focus`): every focus ring, 2px solid.
- **Errata Red** (`error` on `error-bg`): parse and run-time errors, the inline editor note, the error bar.
- **Pass Green** (`ok` on `ok-bg`) and **Not-Yet Copper** (`warn`): challenge verdicts.
- **Execution Highlight** (`exec-line`, `exec-mark`): the line and token the turtle just executed.

### Named Rules
**The Paper Stays Paper Rule.** The drawing sheet is paper in every theme: `sheet` by day, the dimmed `sheet-dark` at night, never inverted. Learners' colours, such as umber `#6b4f2a`, must stay readable exactly as written.

**The Spot Wheel Rule.** A command family keeps one hue wherever it appears: editor highlighting, reference entries, chips. Never colour a family two ways.

**The One Plate Rule.** Exactly one opaque reversed plate per screen: the primary action. Everything else ranks by weight, rule and position.

## Typography

**Display and UI Font:** Archivo Variable (self-hosted; widths 62–125%), falling back to system-ui.
**Code Font:** JetBrains Mono Variable (self-hosted), for the editor, code samples and key caps only.

**Character:** One workhorse grotesque carries everything. Its condensed width (about 80–82%) does the print-label voice: wordmark, titles, imprint and chips. The mono appears only where code is.

### Hierarchy
- **Headline** (750, 1.75rem, 1.2, condensed): page titles such as «Przykłady» and «Pomoc: język Logomocji».
- **Title** (700, 1.375rem, condensed): section openers in the reference and example groups.
- **Doc title** (650, 1.125rem, condensed): the studio's document name (draft, example or challenge).
- **Body** (400, 0.9375rem, 1.5, tabular numerals): UI prose, cards, status.
- **Reading** (400, 1rem, 1.65, up to 74ch): the reference column.
- **Label** (600, 0.8125rem, condensed): chips, meta lines, small buttons.
- **Imprint** (600, 12.5px, 80% width): the sheet imprint.
- **Code** (JetBrains Mono, 14.5px, 1.65; 16px on phones so iOS does not zoom).

### Named Rules
**The Mono Is For Code Rule.** Monospace sets code, key caps and nothing else; labels and data use condensed Archivo.

## Layout

Desktop is a two-pane studio under a 56px band: the editor pane (about 1.15 parts, at least 380px) and the sheet (1 part), 12px apart on the card ground. The sheet pane keeps 20px of card margin around the sheet so the crop marks sit outside the trim, with the imprint 18px below the sheet. Below 900px everything stacks: sheet first (at least 280px, about 48vh), then the code panel. Below 560px, secondary run buttons become 44px icon buttons and the speed slider takes its own row. Pages (examples, challenges, reference) sit in a 1240px column. The reference uses a 220px sticky contents rail beside a 74ch reading column, and the rail turns into wrapped pills on phones. Spacing follows a 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 scale, with more space above headings than below.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat by default. Depth comes from the physical metaphor: the sheet is the one surface that floats above the card, with a soft paper shadow. Popovers and toasts get a single pop shadow. Panels and cards use a 1px hairline border and no shadow.

### Shadow Vocabulary
- **Paper on card** (`box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(23 34 30 / 0.12), 0 6px 18px rgb(23 34 30 / 0.08)`): the drawing sheet only.
- **Pop** (`box-shadow: 0 6px 24px rgb(23 34 30 / 0.16), 0 1px 3px rgb(23 34 30 / 0.12)`): popovers and toasts.

### Named Rules
**The One Sheet Rule.** Only the drawing sheet casts the paper shadow; elevation is declared once, either border or shadow, never both.

## Shapes

Gently squared print forms: controls at 6px (`md`), panels and cards at 10px (`lg`), chips and key caps at 4px (`sm`), and the sheet at a near-square 1px trim. The three print marks are drawn geometry. Crop marks are 11px hairlines offset 16px outside the trim corners. The registration mark is a 6.5px circle with an 11px cross, at the origin. The fold line is a dash of 7 on 5.

### Named Rules
**The Fold Line Rule.** Dashed means "fold, not cut": the challenge target, a pen-up turtle, the hidden-target toggle. A dash is never decoration.

**The Honest Scale Rule.** Zoom moves along whole ratios (1:50 … 1:1 … 20:1), and the imprint names the current one («skala 2:1»).

## Components

### Buttons
- **Shape:** 6px corners (`md`), 36px tall (40–44px on phones).
- **Plate («Uruchom»):** `plate` fill, `paper` text, with a green play glyph; hover lightens the plate. Only one per screen.
- **Default:** `paper` fill, 1px `rule-2` border, `ink` text; hover `paper-2`, active `paper-3`. Disabled keeps the shape at 70% opacity with `ink-3` text.
- **Quiet:** transparent, `ink-2` text, `paper-3` on hover; used for file actions, challenge tools and «Wypróbuj».

### Segmented mode switch
- **Style:** a `paper-2` track with a 1px `rule-2` border and 2px inset. The active segment is `ok-bg` with `fam-move` text and a 1px inner ring.
- **State:** `aria-pressed`; locked (disabled, with a tooltip) during a challenge.

### Sheet tools
A joined row of 36px icon buttons on the sheet colour, ringed by `sheet-rule-strong`, at the sheet's top right: zoom out, zoom in, fit, default 3D view, grid toggle (dimmed when off).

### The sheet imprint (signature)
One condensed line below the trim: document name (bold), mode, «skala» ratio, segment count, then a colour-control bar of the pen colours actually used (13px squares with a hairline edge), then the turtle's position and heading (or «pisak podniesiony»).

### Editor
CodeMirror on `paper` with a `paper-2` gutter. Command words take their family hue at weight 650. Names are italic `tok-name`, comments italic `tok-comment`, brackets bold punctuation. A colour literal is underlined 4px in its own colour. The error is a wavy `error` underline on the token, an `error-bg` line, and an inline note below the line pointing at the column. The executed line is `exec-line` with an `exec-mark` token.

### Cards (examples and challenges)
A fixed anatomy on `paper` with a 1px `rule` border and 10px corners: a sheet-coloured thumbnail (7:5), name (condensed 700), one-line note, meta chips (mode, count or state), and one action. Challenge thumbnails show the target in fold lines.

### Navigation
White labels in the green band. Hover darkens the band behind the link. The current page gets a darker field and a 2px white bar beneath the label, and wraps to a scrollable second row on phones.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do:
- **Do** keep the drawing sheet paper-coloured in both themes (`sheet` / `sheet-dark`).
- **Do** colour a command family with its one hue everywhere (`fam-move`, `fam-turn`, `fam-pen`, `fam-control`, `fam-define`).
- **Do** reserve the reversed plate (`plate`) for the single primary action on a screen.
- **Do** use dashed fold lines (7 on 5) only for pen-up, targets and other not-drawn states.
- **Do** keep text at or above `ink-3` contrast (4.5:1) on every paper and band surface.
- **Do** name zoom as a whole ratio in the imprint.

### Don't:
- **Don't** invert or tint the sheet to match the dark theme; dim it instead.
- **Don't** add gradients, grain, glass or extra shadows; the sheet's paper shadow is the only lift.
- **Don't** use monospace outside code and key caps.
- **Don't** add a second reversed plate or a second accent colour to chrome.
- **Don't** put a coloured side stripe on cards, alerts or notes; state uses a tinted field with a full hairline border.

lines: A restrained neutral system tinted green-grey, with one committed band and a spot-colour wheel that does real jobs: command families, axes, states.
-- **Turtle Ink Green** (`band`): the header band behind the wordmark and navigation, and the turtle's default pen. In dark mode the band deepens to `band-dark`; the pen colour never changes.

+- **Turtle Ink Green** (`band`): the header band behind the wordmark and navigation, and the turtle's default pen. In dark mode the band deepens to `band-dark`; the pen colour never changes. Hover and current-page fields inside the band darken it (`band-shade`, `band-shade-strong`) rather than lighten it, so white labels keep 4.5:1.
- **Key-Line Ink Plate** (`plate`): the single reversed plate on a screen, the «Uruchom» button. In dark mode the plate inverts to `plate-dark` with dark text.
- **Printed Paper** (`paper`, `paper-2`, `paper-3`): editor panel, toolbars and gutter, then hover and inline-code fills.
- **Key-Line Ink** (`ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`): text, secondary text and tertiary text. `ink-3` is the lightest text allowed and holds 4.5:1 on paper and gutter.
-- **The Sheet** (`sheet`, `sheet-dark`, `sheet-rule`, `sheet-ghost`): the drawing surface, its grid and the dashed challenge target.

+- **The Sheet** (`sheet`, `sheet-dark`, `sheet-rule`, `sheet-ghost`, `sheet-ink-3`, `sheet-hover`): the drawing surface, its grid, the dashed challenge target, and the sheet tools. These stay light-theme values in both themes because the sheet never inverts.
- **Errata Red** (`error` on `error-bg`): parse and run-time errors, the inline editor note, the error bar.
- **Pass Green** (`ok` on `ok-bg`) and **Not-Yet Copper** (`warn`): challenge verdicts.
- **Execution Highlight** (`exec-line`, `exec-mark`): the line and token the turtle just executed.
+- **Notice** (`notice-ink` on `notice-bg`, `notice-rule` border): informational notes printed on the sheet, such as "3D view off" or "loading the 3D view".

**The Paper Stays Paper Rule.** The drawing sheet is paper in every theme: `sheet` by day, the dimmed `sheet-dark` at night, never inverted. Learners' colours, such as umber `#6b4f2a`, must stay readable exactly as written.

-Gently squared print forms: controls at 6px (`md`), panels and cards at 10px (`lg`), chips and key caps at 4px (`sm`), and the sheet at a near-square 1px trim. The three print marks are drawn geometry. Crop marks are 11px hairlines offset 16px outside the trim corners. The registration mark is a 6.5px circle with an 11px cross, at the origin. The fold line is a dash of 7 on 5.

+Gently squared print forms: controls at 6px (`md`), panels and cards at 10px (`lg`), chips, key caps and small marks at 4px (`sm`), the sheet at a near-square 1px trim (`sheet`), and pills (`pill`) only for the reference's contents links on phones. The three print marks are drawn geometry. Crop marks are 11px hairlines offset 16px outside the trim corners. The registration mark is a 6.5px circle with an 11px cross, at the origin. The fold line is a dash of 7 on 5.
**The Fold Line Rule.** Dashed means "fold, not cut": the challenge target, a pen-up turtle, the hidden-target toggle. A dash is never decoration.

content.text:
Logomocja is built in `/work`: all 11 features, the full language and the delivery contract. `bun install`, `bun run build` and `bun run test` pass from a clean checkout (109 tests). I never saw the interface rendered: the container has no browser. So the finish review stopped at `disposition: recapture`, and the design is unreviewed against real screenshots.

**What's there**
- **Stack:** Vite and TypeScript with no UI framework, CodeMirror 6 for the editor, and three.js for 3D, which loads only when WebGL works.
- **Language:** the interpreter executes one command at a time, so run, step, pause, resume and reset share one engine.
- **Editor:**
  - colours each command family in its own hue;
  - underlines colour literals in their own colour;
  - shows the Polish error message inline under the faulty line;
  - highlights the line just executed.
- **Editing while running:** typing during a run stops it and keeps what was drawn.
- **2D sheet:** pan, wheel, pinch and keyboard zoom, fit, and an origin marker. Zoom moves in whole ratios like "skala 2:1".
- **3D view:** orbit, pan, zoom, a default-view button, a ground grid and axes. Without WebGL it says why and shows a still angled view of the drawing.
- **Content:**
  - the 13 standard programs, byte for byte, also openable by name (`#/przyklady/gwiazda`);
  - 10 auto-checked challenges, with the target shown as dashed lines;
  - a Polish command reference with a runnable example for every command.
- **Sharing and safety:** permalinks, PNG export, `.logo` download and open, and per-mode drafts. Loading anything over your own draft saves it to a "Kopie" list with a one-click restore, so nothing is lost silently.

**Testing approach:** tests sit at the four approved seams: `run()`, the execution controller, the challenge checker, and the whole app booted in happy-dom (a headless DOM). Most cycles went red then green. Some app tests passed on their first run because the first app slice already wired those controls; I've said so rather than counting them as red-first. Where a test passed only by accident (stray-value and 2D pitch messages), I tightened it until it failed.

**Other checks**
- The production bundle, built under `BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/`, ran in happy-dom. `open()` matched `run()` for all 13 programs, and every asset loaded from a plain static server at that path.
- The real 2D drawing code rendered to PNGs with a headless canvas library installed outside the project. That caught a flat projection that drew the cube as an ambiguous hexagon.
- I checked the 3D turtle's orientation numerically and fixed a mirrored-orientation bug.
- Working out contrast by hand found three spots below the accessibility minimum (navigation links, their hover, line numbers), now fixed.

**Not verified**
- How the pages look and lay out in a real browser, on desktop or phone.
- The three.js view on screen.
- PNG export and real touch gestures.

**Impeccable and process notes**
- PRODUCT.md is inferred from the brief, with each inferred fact labelled, since no interview channel was in scope.
- The direction roll assigned my seventh grounded candidate: a printed cut-and-fold model sheet in the *Mały Modelarz* tradition. The six dealt challengers were all declined, and each one's useful discipline was written into the direction contract.
- The finish reviewer and documenter ran in-thread from the skill's fallback instructions, because delegated agents were unavailable. The review record is in `.impeccable/review/finish-review.md`.
- DESIGN.md and `.impeccable/design.json` describe the built system, and the design detector reports no findings. Its browser-based scan couldn't run, so that result is an undercount.
- I skipped the skill's update offer as the benchmark instructed, kept telemetry off, and made no commits.

README.md covers running, building, testing, the project layout and these limits in more detail.
